key_insight: The paper shows how to use a limited annotation budget to optimally choose which sequential outcomes to label, enabling lower-variance off-policy evaluation when rewards are partially missing or expensive to obtain.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical annotation strategy for real-world AI systems that rely on noisy text/image labels, helping engineers and scientists get trustworthy policy estimates without fully expert-labeling every sample.
method: Formulate off-policy evaluation with missing rewards using doubly robust estimation.
Derive variance-optimal annotation probabilities for sequential forward-monotone annotation protocols.
Provide a batch-adaptive implementation that is feasible under a limited ground-truth labeling budget.
evidence_signal: In simulations and two real datasets, the method reduced RMSE by 34–65% on housing-placement tasks and 17–68% on housing-application progress at 40% annotation budget and above, and by 55–62% across all budgets on LMArena.
watch_item: The approach depends on a carefully designed sequential annotation protocol and its benefits may be reduced if the missingness/annotation process is poorly modeled or operational constraints prevent adaptive labeling.
paper_title: Optimal Sequential Annotations for Off-Policy Evaluation
